PEP: 10.0 flow with $211M dark pool — staples being aggressively bid alongside KO
GE: $281M dark pool + 9.85 blocks — industrial leader seeing top-tier institutional sponsorship
META: $41M near-money call premium + $671M dark pool — largest mega-cap tape print on the board
AMZN: $22M call premium + $568M dark pool — consumer/cloud accumulation
GOOGL/GOOG: combined ~$1.2B dark pool with strong call flow — dual-class accumulation pattern
NFLX: $10M call premium + $311M dark pool — media leader bid

MU: $33M call premium (9.35 flow) — strongest near-money call tape in memory chips
AXP: $489M dark pool with 10.0 blocks — financial accumulation standout

MS: flow 1.28 — divergence from GS bullish setup signals selective financials positioning
KLAC: flow 2.29 — semicap outlier vs LRCX/AMAT bullish prints
PG: flow 1.12 — staples divergence vs KO/PEP strength
WMT: flow 2.34 — retail distribution alongside HD
UNH: flow 2.52 — managed care continues to see put-side positioning
IBM: flow 2.70 — legacy tech being faded

narrative.rotation_signal: Accumulation is broad across mega-cap tech (META, AMZN, GOOGL, NFLX), semicap equipment (LRCX, AMAT), memory (MU), and defensive staples (KO, PEP). Distribution is concentrated in retail (HD, WMT), managed care (UNH), legacy tech (IBM, CSCO), and select semis (AMD, KLAC) — suggesting rotation INTO leadership names and OUT OF lagging consumer/healthcare/legacy exposure.
narrative.diverging_from_industry_layer: Semis are split — MU/LRCX/AMAT bullish while AMD/KLAC bearish, signaling selective rather than sector-wide chip positioning. Financials similarly split: GS/AXP bullish, MS bearish. Staples diverge from defensive narrative: KO/PEP heavily bid while PG/WMT distributed.
